area: Flash/AS3 animation semantics for transcription (SESSION 24 A12.3: run_sheathed, death, hit reaction) — adversarial verification

item_verdicts.title: Frame-level r="1" flag exists in the payload and the transcriber silently drops it — including in already-committed balancedhorizontalslash_partc
item_verdicts.why: The FACTS reproduce exactly under my own probe of reference/extracted/bindata/108_1t4635s0.bin: frame attrs are Counter({'i': 1638, 'r': 89}); all 89 r values are "1"; they fall across exactly 25 anims (heavyjumpslash_parta ×6 [f4-9], gangnam ×43, stabattack [2,3], launchopponent [4,10], mining ×12, ...), and balancedhorizontalslash_partc frame i=5 is one of them. transcribeAnims.py's `<f i="(\d+)"[^>]*>` swallows it while `known = set(kv) - {...}` fail-louds on <n>; the byte-check in tests/a11AnimData.test.ts uses the SAME permissive frame regex (`/<f i="(\d+)"[^>]*>([\s\S]*?)<\/f>/g`), so nothing in the repo could ever catch the loss. Wahlers source verified live and says exactly what is attributed to it ("The Flash Player uses the value of the Ratio field to determine whether or not to reset the playhead in the placed Sprite to frame 1"; spec's morph-only wording is "incorrect"). WHAT FAILS: the item's central recommendation — 'treat its semantics as an open question' — is refuted by the repo's own decompiled-AS3 documentation, which the research never opened.
item_verdicts.correction: r="1" is NOT an open question and NOT a playhead-reset/keyframe marker. docs/research/fidelity/FIGHTER_ART_IDS.md §3 already records the AS3 semantics from `§1t59s0§.reorderLayers`: "z-order is creation order (slot 0 at the back) *unless* the frame carries `r="1"`, in which case the node list order wins. Note `§1t59s0§`'s constructor pushes nodes in **reverse** document order." Two consequences the item gets backwards: (1) a dense 19-node frame is where the flag matters MOST, not where it is 'indistinguishable' — the whole layering flips; (2) composePose draws strictly in slot order (`slotShapes.forEach((shapes, slot) => ...)`), so balancedhorizontalslash_partc frame 5 is rendering with the wrong z-order in the committed build TODAY. Implement the documented rule (record the flag, then order parts by node-list order — reverse-document — on r-frames), do not 'grade its behavior against video'.

item_verdicts.title: Flash Matrix column semantics (x'=a·x+c·y+tx, y'=b·x+d·y+ty) — repo's planPose already applies the exact AS3 formula, and /100 is the right divisor
item_verdicts.why: Repo check passes term-for-term: src/core/planPose.ts — "/** The 2×2 half of a Flash matrix: x' = a·x + c·y, y' = b·x + d·y. */" and `m = { a: cos, b: sin, c: -sin, d: cos }`; src/core/composePose.ts divides all four by OG_MATRIX_UNITS; src/config/ogPose.ts `export const OG_MATRIX_UNITS = 100`. Sources all live (200). The Adobe/airsdk Matrix pages support the [a c tx / b d ty] layout (a/c position pixels along x, b/d along y, "u and v are 0.0, w is 1.0") though neither prints the algebraic formula verbatim; m2osw supplies the cos/sin form (SWFmatrix11 = Sx·cos, 12 = Sy·sin, 21 = −Sx·sin, 22 = Sy·cos) — it labels skew0/skew1 the opposite way round to the item, but the item's labelling (b = RotateSkew0, c = RotateSkew1) is the one that matches the SWF MATRIX record, so the source is the loose party, not the claim. STRONGEST corroboration is the payload itself: death's 6 matrix nodes are orthonormal only after ÷100 and only approximately — f11 {a:63,b:−77,c:77,d:63} gives |col|=0.995, det=0.990; f34 {a:−4,b:99,c:−100,d:−4} gives 0.991/1.001 — i.e. the 2-dp quantization loss is demonstrably IN THE SOURCE, exactly as claimed. Nothing to change.

item_verdicts.title: A12.3 targets probed byte-level: run_sheathed and death parse cleanly under the existing grammar; the whole payload has NO color transforms, motion guides, labels, or scripts
item_verdicts.why: Census reproduced exactly: tags Counter({'n':49004,'f':3276,'anim':316,'animdata':2}) = 4 element types, 158 anims / 1638 frames / 24502 nodes; anim attrs only {i,d,l(38)}; node attrs only i,x,y (24502 each), r (24010), a/b/c/d (492 each) — no color-transform attrs, no labels, no scripts, no guides. run_sheathed: d=9, l="1", frames [19×9], 0 matrix nodes, 0 r-frames. death: d=38, non-looping, frames [19×38], 6 matrix nodes, 0 r-frames, slots [0-7,9-16,18-20] identical to walk and idle. sheathesword [19,8,8,8,8,0,0] with 5 matrices and sheathetoidle [19,8×7] with 7 matrices — the sparse-plus-matrix claim is right too. ADOPT verified EMPIRICALLY, not by inspection: I ran a copy of scripts/anim/transcribeAnims.py with "run_sheathed" and "death" appended to ANIMS against the real bindata; it emitted both anims (1853-line output, `run_sheathed:` and `death:` blocks, union type extended) with zero FATALs. §S24-F does carry the red-wash rows the note points at ("Full-screen red WASH = player-took-damage feedback (3–5 ticks/burst...)"). Cross-check: docs/research/fidelity/FIGHTER_ART_IDS.md §3 independently lists `run_sheathed` and `death` among "poses the duel needs, all present".

item_verdicts.title: No dedicated 'hit reaction' clip exists in the payload — map §S24-F's three measured reactions to the gotlaunched/downed/brake clip family from video before transcribing
item_verdicts.why: Inventory confirmed: a name scan of all 158 anims returns zero hit/hurt/flinch/react clips, and every candidate named exists (gotlaunchedupwards_parta/b/c, gotlauncheddowned, gotlauncheddownedend, downed, downedup, downedup2, flipupfromdowned, brake, defeatedanimationv1/v2, launchopponent). §S24-F's three-reaction row reads as quoted. Evidence crops exist (reference/frames/session24/reach-B-honda-duel/, 248 files; the §S24 header line names "B Honda Shizuka VS duel t=3770–3782", so the window attribution is sound). MEASURE_FIRST stands. Two ledger-fidelity defects need fixing before anyone acts on the numbers.
item_verdicts.correction: (1) UNITS: the ledger says "small hits (−7/−12 px HP) displace ~0; big hits (−17..−19) displace 40–270 px" — those are HP-BAR PIXEL drops, not HP/damage points. Do not carry "−7/−12 HP" into any damage config. (2) The −188 px knockback figure is contested by the §S24-H Verify-pass corrections (2026-08-12), which re-measure the point-blank hit it derives from: popup reads 17 (not −19), "Honda's displacement is +309 px by plate, not 188", and the f0149–0152 flash is "most plausibly the PLAYER being hit" — i.e. both the magnitude and the actor attribution of the 188 knockback are unsettled. Use ~309 px for the point-blank knockback and treat the player-side −188 slide as unconfirmed until re-measured. (3) Minor: the candidate list omits `deathdowned`, which is also in the payload and is reaction-shaped.

item_verdicts.title: deathbyarrow introduces slot 21 — the only anim beyond the 0-20 slot map; add a slot-range fail-loud before the death-variant anims
item_verdicts.why: Payload-wide probe: slots present = [0-7, 9-16, 18-21]; slots 8 and 17 appear ZERO times across all 24502 nodes (the alias guard is validated against the full payload, as claimed); the only anim carrying a slot >20 is deathbyarrow (21 frames × 20 nodes, slot 21 in every frame). death itself is unaffected (standard 19-slot set). transcribeAnims.py's only slot guard is `if kv["i"] in (8, 17)` — no upper bound. src/config/ogPose.ts documents "Nodes exist for slots 0–7, 9–16 and 18–20", and planPose.ts throws `planPose: slot ${slot} needs shape ${shapeId}, which was not supplied` — both quoted accurately. One refinement that STRENGTHENS the item rather than weakening it: the claim's hedge "throw (or silently drop)" resolves to DROP — OG_DRESSED_SLOT_SHAPES is `OG_SLOT_SHAPES.map(...)` (indices 0-20) and composePose iterates `slotShapes.forEach`, so a slot-21 node is silently discarded with no error anywhere. That makes the transcription-time fail-loud more necessary, not less.

item_verdicts.title: The 15 fps latch + carry-forward player is the correct Flash playback model — validated against Flash timeline semantics, no changes warranted
item_verdicts.why: Pillars (2) and (3) survive intact and the repo does implement what is described (src/core/ogAnimPlayer.ts: ANIM_TIMING.poseStepMs whole-step latch, the `carried` Map overlay with the partc 19,0,19,0,19,19,7 example in its header, `advanceOne` hold-last-frame; src/game/DuelScene.ts `fighterPose` owns the a→b→c chain — verified). The Wahlers source genuinely supports the parent-controlled-playhead pillar. But pillar (1) — the claim that SHS Duels has "a 15 fps document setting" proven by the 60 fps burst — is dead on two independent counts, one of them a PRIMARY SOURCE inside this repo. Its adjudication ("no changes warranted") therefore cannot stand as validated.
item_verdicts.correction: The OG's document frame rate is 24 fps, not 15. reference/extracted/payload.xml's own SWF header reads `<swf ... frameCount="6" frameRate="24.0" version="17">` — a decompiler-extracted primary source that outranks any video inference. Separately, the §S24-H Verify-pass block (2026-08-12) kills the cited proof outright: "The 60 fps '4-frame content block' defence is VOID — that is a property of the capture (§00), not of the game", and §00 itself already said the 4-frame runs are "a property of the *archival capture*, not necessarily of the Flash game (which likely ran 24–30 fps)". src/config/anim.ts labels `poseStepMs: 1000 / 15` MEASURED off exactly that voided 4-frame video cadence. So: keep the whole-step latch, the carry-forward map and the caller-owned chaining, but re-open the STEP RATE as a live question (24 fps ⇒ walk d=20 runs 0.83 s, not 1.33 s; death d=38 runs 1.58 s, not 2.53 s — a ~60% timing error across every transcribed clip). Minor source note: the kirupa page confirms "the default frame rate is set to 24" in later Flash but did not surface the item's "12 fps historically" half.

overall_note: Sources: all 6 distinct URLs are live (200) and the two I fetched in depth say what is attributed to them — Wahlers is a strong match (ratio field is spec'd morph-only but \"also applies to Sprite characters\" and controls playhead reset); the Adobe/airsdk Matrix pages support the a c tx / b d ty layout but never print the x'/y' formula verbatim (the cos/sin comes from the B-grade m2osw page, which labels skew0/skew1 opposite to the SWF spec). No fabricated or dead citation found. Payload-side, every byte-level number in the report reproduced exactly under independent probing (158/1638/24502; 89 r-frames across 25 anims; run_sheathed d=9, death d=38 with 6 matrices; deathbyarrow's unique slot 21), and the ADOPT was proven by actually running the transcriber with both names appended. TWO FINDINGS THE RESEARCH MISSED, both from repo primary sources it never opened: (1) docs/research/fidelity/FIGHTER_ART_IDS.md §3 already documents the r=\"1\" semantics from the decompiled AS3 `reorderLayers` — it is a Z-ORDER OVERRIDE (node-list order, reverse-document, wins over creation order), not a playhead reset; this makes the committed balancedhorizontalslash_partc frame 5 a live rendering defect since composePose always draws in slot order, and it means the flag matters MOST on dense frames, the opposite of the report's reasoning. (2) reference/extracted/payload.xml's SWF header says frameRate=\"24.0\", which refutes the \"15 fps document setting\" premise of the last item and puts src/config/anim.ts's `poseStepMs: 1000/15` (labelled MEASURED off the video cadence the 2026-08-12 verify pass voided) in question for every clip A12.3 is about to transcribe — the highest-value correction in this review. Net: 3 CONFIRMED, 3 WEAKENED, 0 REFUTED; the transcription plan (append run_sheathed + death, add a slot>20 guard, don't renormalize matrices, recreate red wash scene-side) is safe to execute once the r=\"1\" z-order rule is implemented rather than deferred.
